I've now read the full pipeline and every function it invokes. Here's the complete, ordered trace for **`POST /api/owners`** (defined in `owners.POST.yml`). Every step runs inside a single `transaction` governance, so all writes commit once at the end (or roll back together on escalation).

## Gate (before any step)

- **Authorization** — `composition.authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"` guards the whole file. No role → `AuthorizationDeniedException` → **403 Forbidden**.

## Validations & side-effects, in pipeline order

1. **`validate` → `ValidateOwner`** — binds `@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto` and runs bean validation (this is the one and only body read). Constraints from the DTO:
   - `firstName`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern ^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$`
   - `lastName`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..30)`, `@Pattern ^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}\.?$`
   - `address`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..255)`
   - `city`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..80)`
   - `telephone`: `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..20)`
   - `email` (optional): `@Email`, `@Size(max 255)`
   - `registrationDate`, `sharesHousehold`: optional
   
   Failure → `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → **400**. On success it republishes the DTO as a variable for later steps. *(It runs first deliberately so an invalid body is a 400 rather than being masked by a later check.)*

2. **`normalize` → `NormalizeOwnerTelephone`** — converts `telephone` to E.164 (`OwnerTelephones.toE164`: strip spaces/dashes/brackets; keep a leading `+`/country code, else assume `+61` and drop one leading `0`; require 8–15 digits) and **writes it back onto the request in place**. Unconvertible → `InvalidTelephoneException` → **400**.

3. **`normalizeAddress` → `NormalizeOwnerAddress`** — normalizes `address` (`OwnerAddresses.normalize`: trim, collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand `ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`) and **writes it back in place**. Blank after normalization → `InvalidAddressException` → **400**.

4. **`ensureUniqueTelephone` → `EnsureUniqueOwnerTelephone`** — scans **all** existing owners; if any existing owner's telephone (converted to E.164) equals the request's E.164 number → `DuplicateTelephoneException` → **409**.

5. **`ensureUniqueHousehold` → `EnsureUniqueHousehold`** — unless `sharesHousehold == true`, scans all owners; if one matches on normalized last name **and** normalized address (`Households`) → `DuplicateHouseholdException` → **409**. (If `sharesHousehold` is true the check is skipped.)

6. **`ensureCityCapacity` → `EnsureCityCapacity`** — counts existing owners whose `city` exactly equals the request city; if **≥ 50** → `CityAtCapacityException` → **409**.

7. **`ensureDailyLimit` → `EnsureDailyLimit`** — computes the effective business day (supplied `registrationDate` or today, rolled forward over a weekend to Monday — `BusinessDays`), counts existing owners already registered on that day; if **≥ 100** → `DailyLimitExceededException` → **429**.

8. **`build` → `BuildOwner`** — maps the DTO to a new `Owner` (`OwnerMapper.toOwner`, with `id` and `pets` ignored), sets `email` to its lower-cased form (`OwnerEmails.normalize`), and sets `registrationDate` to the effective business day. Publishes the `Owner`.

9. **`assignCustomerCode` → `AssignCustomerCode`** — sets `customerCode` = `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where the 4-digit sequence is `(number of existing owners in that city) + 1` (e.g. `MAD-FRA-0007`).

10. **`assignHousehold` → `AssignHousehold`** — only when `sharesHousehold == true`: derives a `householdId` (first 12 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256 of normalized `lastName\0address`), sets it on the new owner, and **back-fills and `save()`s any existing household members** that lack it. *(This is an extra persistence side-effect on other rows.)* Does nothing (leaves `householdId` null) otherwise.

11. **`countNamesakes` → `CountNamesakes`** — sets `namesakeCount` = number of existing owners sharing the same first + last name, case-insensitively (the new owner excluded, since it isn't saved yet).

12. **`save` → `SaveOwner`** — `ownerRepository.save(owner)` persists the new owner.

13. **`respond` → `RespondWithOwnerCreated`** — maps to `OwnerDto` and returns **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

## Notes

- All counts/uniqueness checks (steps 4–7, 9, 11) read **existing** owners only — the new owner is not yet saved when they run.
- Because every step shares the one `transaction` governance, any escalation after writes (e.g. a `save` failure → `DataIntegrityViolationException`, handled as **409**) rolls the whole request back; nothing is partially committed.
- The error-to-status mapping above is confirmed by the handlers in `rest/escalation/` (400 / 409 / 429 via `ProblemDetails`).

- All counts/uniqueness checks (steps 4–7, 9, 11) read **existing** owners only — the new owner is not yet saved when they run.
- Because every step shares the one `transaction` governance, any escalation after writes (e.g. a `save` failure → `DataIntegrityViolationException`, handled as **409**) rolls the whole request back; nothing is partially committed.
- The error-to-status mapping above is confirmed by the handlers in `rest/escalation/` (400 / 409 / 429 via `ProblemDetails`).
